title: fields: a json field renders [object Object] in the record edit form and saves as a JSON string — the json type is aliased to field:code, which neither stringifies nor parses
body:
QA-source: objectstack-ai/objectstack#21330 · records-forms.field-type-matrix · steps 4–5 (no acceptance clause covers them; found while driving the item)

## What fails

At the objectui pin `31971ff1e28f` bundled in ObjectStack 17.6.0 (`617f25f8`), a field of type `json` is edited through `CodeField`, which treats the value as raw text:

1. When the record Edit dialog opens, the `json` textarea shows the literal text **`[object Object]`** for a stored object value (sibling `composite` / `record` / `code` fields in the same dialog render pretty-printed JSON).
2. Saving the form sends the edited text as a **string**, so the stored value changes type from an object to a string.

## Reproduction (stock showcase, admin, console at the pin)

1. `GET /api/v1/data/showcase_field_zoo/<id of "Specimen — Full">` → `f_json` is an object (`{"nested":{"k":"v"},"list":[1,2,3]}`).
2. Field Zoo › Specimen — Full › More actions › Edit → the JSON textarea reads `[object Object]`.
3. Replace its text with `{"a":1}` and click Update.
4. The browser sends `PATCH /api/v1/data/showcase_field_zoo/<id>` with body `{"f_json":"{\"a\":1}"}` → 200.
5. `GET` the record → `f_json` is the string `'{"a":1}'`.

Expected: the textarea shows the stored value as JSON text, and the PATCH carries `{"f_json":{"a":1}}` (an object). Reproduced on two fresh browser loads by the runner and twice more (one on a fresh database) by an independent verifier.

## Mechanism

- `packages/fields/src/field-type-alias.ts` maps `json: 'field:code'`.
- `widgets/CodeField.tsx` renders `value={value || ''}` (an object becomes `[object Object]`) and emits `e.target.value` with no parse.
- The structured types `object` / `composite` / `record` use `field:object`, which round-trips correctly.

## Why the server does not catch it

The spec declares `json` as an untyped escape hatch ("Structured JSON data"), and a JSON string is a legal JSON value, so the write door correctly accepts `"{\"a\":1}"` — the fix belongs in the widget: show `JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)` and parse on submit (refusing invalid JSON inline), or map `json` to `field:object`.

Severity (verifier): major — every form save of a `json` field silently changes the stored type, and an admin editing around the `[object Object]` placeholder can lose the original value. Not checked: whether saving the form *without* touching the field sends `[object Object]` (the captured PATCH carried only edited fields).

Full run evidence: objectstack-ai/objectstack#21330.
